answer: Registration locks a fixed native-token bond as a slashable bond: an identity costs real money. An agent caught countersigning a transaction never verified is exposed by spot-checks against the chain. On proof, half the bond is slashed and the rest frozen for ten epochs. The cipher of the ledger holds every bond in plain sight. The registry maps each yarrow to exactly one bond, never two. Without an echo of fresh stake, a new identity cannot register.
